location: England, Norfolk, Caistor Saint Edmund, Harford Farm
description: A somewhat mysterious site. A series of six rectangular enclosures following a line of Bronze Age barrows, little to suggest agricultural or occupational use, so it has been suggested they may be mortuary enclosures. Though only one cremation nearby was found, so the possibility of them being shrines has been put forward. Roughly dated to Late Iron Age - Early Roman
bibliography: Ashwin, T, and S Bates. “Southern Norwich By-Pass, Part 1: Excavations at Bixley, Casitor St Edmunds.” East Anglian Archaeology 91 (2000).
Gurney, D. “Settlement, Religion and Industry on the Roman Fen Edge.” Norfolk East Anglian Archaeology 31 (1986).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Harford Farm, Caistor St Edmund (Norfolk).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
